sections.html:
Three roads lead to a sale here: an agent listing, a do-it-yourself sale, or a cash deal made directly with a buyer. If the clock is ticking, weigh the cash figure against repair bills and the weeks a listing might sit. Get any offer on paper, and ask what the buyer's inspection could do to the number.

A local quirk comes up first. Burleson is split by the Johnson and Tarrant county line. Your parcel's own tax statement names the clerk, appraisal district and tax office that apply. Read it before you order title work or request a payoff, since mixing up counties costs days.

Burleson is a suburb south of Fort Worth with more than 55,000 residents. Interstate 35W passes through, roughly 15 miles south of downtown Fort Worth and 40 miles southwest of Dallas. Commuters, families and investors all shop here. More than 20 parks and a Historic Old Town give the city its local anchors.

A newer subdivision and an older house by Old Town can land at very different prices. Find out which comparable sales a buyer used.

sections.h2: Older houses near the original townsite
sections.html:
Burleson dates to 1881, the year the Missouri, Kansas and Texas railroad came through, and it became a city in 1912. For decades only a few hundred people lived here, so most of what stands today went up in later growth years. Houses near the original townsite, though, can be about a century old.

Expect a buyer to price the usual age items: electrical panels that need updating, galvanized plumbing that needs replacing, and slabs or piers that need a look. Having an inspection or repair estimate in hand can keep that discussion short.

A permit is required here. Under Chapter 14, Article XII of the city code, any residence rented as lodging for one to thirty consecutive days is a short-term rental, and running one without a permit is unlawful. Sellers should note that the permit stays behind: it does not move to a new owner.

Burleson short-term rental permit rules
TopicRule
Permit termExpires on the last day of the month one year after issue
Renewal filingOpens 30 days before expiration
InspectionOn site, within 10 days of notice from the city
Changes to the applicationReported within 10 days
Fine, no culpable mental stateUp to $500
Fine, fire safety or public health offense with a culpable mental stateUp to $2,000

Anyone buying the house to rent it short term starts a new application. The code also provides an affirmative defense when an occupant is a party to the sale and remains under a written post-closing occupancy agreement.

Value is fixed as of January 1 by whichever appraisal district covers the parcel, and taxing units set rates later. No state property tax exists in Texas. The October bill is payable on arrival. For most owners the real cutoff is January 31, because February 1 begins delinquency.

  • A late bill draws six percent penalty and one percent interest in February, and the penalty climbs through July 1.
  • The taxing unit's collection lawyer may add as much as 20 percent.
  • Homeowners can pay half by November 30 and half by June 30.
  • Owners over 65, or disabled, may pick four installments instead.

Ask the Johnson County or Tarrant County tax office for your exact payoff before you close.

sections.h2: Late taxes or a value that looks too high
sections.html:
Being late isn't the end of the road. Certain collectors allow delinquent tax to be paid over as many as 36 months, and a homestead owner can demand a plan. A written request to waive penalty and interest is possible too, with tight deadlines, so talk to the collector soon.

  • Protest a value with the appraisal review board, whose deadline falls around May 15.
  • A ruling against you can still be taken to court or arbitration.
  • Appealing doesn't excuse you from paying the undisputed tax by the delinquency date.
  • The lien attaches January 1 and rides with the land, so a buyer will insist the balance be cleared.

Carry the appraisal notice and your latest bill to every sale conversation. Those two papers tell a buyer what holding the house costs.

Most Texas foreclosures skip the courtroom and run on the deed of trust's power of sale. A default notice from the servicer begins the process, and the lender next puts a sale notice up at the courthouse and files it with the county clerk. Look at the Johnson County or Tarrant County clerk, depending on where the house sits.

The auction happens on the first Tuesday of a month, starting at the hour in the notice and never more than three hours past it. If the sale leaves a shortfall, the lender has two years to sue for it, and the borrower may ask for a fair market value offset. Selling beforehand generally costs less than an auction.

sections.h2: Tenants in a house you want to sell
sections.html:
Texas landlords begin with a written notice to vacate. Three days applies unless the lease sets another period. After that the landlord files in justice court, where the hearing is set 10 to 21 days out. Five days after judgment is the tenant's appeal window.

A writ of possession can't come sooner than six days after judgment, and it generally expires 60 days out. If the tenant is staying, spell out in your contract who keeps the lease and the security deposit.

After you accept an offer, the title company pulls the tax record from the right county, confirms the loan balance and hunts for liens. Those get paid out of your proceeds on closing day, and the clerk records the deed you sign. Before then, find out whether a short-term rental permit exists and say so in the contract, since a buyer can't take it over. Cancel utilities only after the keys change hands.

Hold on to the settlement statement. A fall or winter closing can leave that year's tax bill arriving after you move, so leave the title company a forwarding address.

Collect a few papers first: the tax statement, a mortgage payoff figure, any lease, and the rental permit and tax records if guests stayed. With those on the table a cash buyer can quote quickly, and the title company can start its search without chasing you. Then confirm closing costs in writing, and ask the title company whether any tax or lien item would shrink your net.

faqs.q: Is Burleson in Johnson County or Tarrant County?
faqs.a: Both. The line runs through the city, and your parcel's side of it picks the clerk, appraisal district and tax office. A tax statement or county map settles it.

faqs.q: Can a buyer keep my Burleson short-term rental permit?
faqs.a: No. Under the city code a permit can't be transferred or assigned, so a new owner applies from scratch and has to pass the on-site inspection.

faqs.q: How much penalty applies to late Burleson property tax?
faqs.a: It starts at six percent on February 1 and reaches 12 percent by July. Interest and any collection lawyer fee come on top, so settle it or arrange a plan early.

faqs.q: What is the shortest timeline from a Texas default notice to an auction?
faqs.a: The borrower has 20 days to reinstate after the default notice, and the auction needs 21 days of sale notice. A private sale fits in that span.

faqs.q: What fine applies to an unpermitted Burleson short-term rental?
faqs.a: An ordinary violation is a Class C misdemeanor, up to $500. A fire-safety or public-health offense charged with a culpable mental state can reach $2,000. Ask the city for its current schedule.
